issues.legal_issue: A transferee who relies on part performance must demonstrate readiness and willingness to perform the agreement and acts of part performance referable to that agreement.
material_facts: The parties agreed to a sale for a price of 17,000, and the transferee paid 12,000 and took possession under the agreement.
The transferee maintained that the agreed price was only 12,000 and did not pay the remaining 5,000 despite a demand for payment.
The transferee relied on part performance to resist the transferor’s claim for possession.
issues.conclusion: The transferee was not entitled to protection based on part performance because he was not ready and willing to perform the agreement alleged by the transferor; possession alone did not establish part performance of that agreement.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 53A of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, a transferee must be ready and willing to perform the agreement. Acts relied on as part performance must be referable to the alleged agreement and not to another title, and must be unequivocally referable to an agreement of the kind alleged. Part performance operates as a shield to protect possession, not as a sword.

rule.if: appeal_from_possession_decree and transferee_claimed_part_performance and transferee_denied_agreed_contract_terms and transferee_left_balance_unpaid

predicates.appeal_from_possession_decree: The proceeding is an appeal concerning a decree for possession of property.
predicates.transferee_claimed_part_performance: The transferee relied on acts said to constitute part performance of an agreement.
predicates.transferee_denied_agreed_contract_terms: The transferee denied the contract terms on which the transferor relied.
predicates.transferee_left_balance_unpaid: The transferee did not pay the balance claimed to be due under those terms.
predicates.part_performance_protection_unavailable: The transferee cannot obtain protection of possession on the basis of part performance.

issues.definition: When a transferee relying on part performance denies the asserted contract terms and leaves the claimed balance unpaid in an appeal concerning possession, the transferee cannot obtain protection of possession on that basis.

issues.legal_issue: A factual finding that the time for performance was extended cannot stand when the issue was not specifically raised and the parties did not try it.
material_facts: The High Court found that the time for performance had been extended by one year.
No specific issue concerning an extension was raised, and the parties did not go to trial on that question.
issues.conclusion: The finding that time for performance had been extended was erroneous and could not be relied on.
issues.legal_principle: Questions of fact should be framed as specific issues so that the parties know what is to be tried; a court should not decide a factual question on which the parties did not go to trial.

rule.if: appeal_from_decree and lower_appellate_court_found_extension and no_specific_issue_on_extension and parties_did_not_try_extension

predicates.appeal_from_decree: The proceeding is an appeal from a decree.
predicates.lower_appellate_court_found_extension: The lower appellate court found that the time for performance had been extended.
predicates.no_specific_issue_on_extension: No specific factual issue about an extension was framed.
predicates.parties_did_not_try_extension: The parties did not go to trial on whether time had been extended.
predicates.extension_finding_unsustainable: The finding that time was extended cannot stand.

issues.definition: If a lower appellate court finds an extension in an appeal from a decree despite the absence of a specific issue and trial of that question, the extension finding cannot stand.

issues.legal_issue: A respondent may support a judgment on an available ground but cannot challenge an adverse finding without filing a cross-objection.
material_facts: The High Court found that the agreement price was 17,000.
The respondent sought to challenge that finding in the appeal but had not filed a cross-objection against it.
issues.conclusion: The respondent could not challenge the finding about the agreement price, although a respondent may support the judgment on a ground available under it.
issues.legal_principle: A respondent may support the judgment under appeal on any ground open under that judgment, but an adverse finding cannot be challenged without a cross-objection.

predicates.appeal_from_judgment: The proceeding is an appeal from a judgment.
predicates.respondent_challenged_adverse_finding: The respondent sought to contest a finding adverse to the respondent in the judgment under appeal.
predicates.respondent_filed_no_cross_objection: The respondent did not file a cross-objection against that finding.
predicates.challenge_to_adverse_finding_not_permitt: The respondent cannot challenge the adverse finding in the appeal.

issues.definition: In an appeal from a judgment, a respondent who challenges an adverse finding without filing a cross-objection cannot contest that finding.

issues.legal_issue: An objection to the competence of an appellate certificate based on valuation cannot be raised for the first time at a late stage.
material_facts: The respondent contended that the certificate was incompetent because the value had not exceeded the relevant threshold.
The respondent had not raised the objection when the matter was heard in the High Court or in the statement of case.
issues.conclusion: The valuation objection to the certificate could not be raised at that late stage.
issues.legal_principle: An objection to valuation cannot be raised at a late stage; the Court followed State of Assam and Anr. v. Basanta Kumar Dass and Ors. The Court also relied on the unfairness of allowing a late objection when the other party could have addressed it in the High Court.

predicates.appeal_on_certificate: The proceeding is an appeal brought under an appellate certificate.
predicates.respondent_raises_valuation_objection_la: The respondent raises a valuation objection to the certificate at a late stage.
predicates.respondent_raised_no_earlier_objection: The respondent did not raise the objection in the earlier proceedings or in the statement of case.
predicates.late_valuation_objection_not_permitted: The valuation objection cannot be considered at that late stage.

issues.definition: When a respondent first raises a valuation objection to an appellate certificate at a late stage after raising no earlier objection, the objection cannot be considered.

issues.legal_issue: A party may sue for relief when the other party has refused to perform the agreement.
material_facts: The transferor alleged that the agreed price was 17,000 and that the transferee had failed to pay the balance after demand.
The transferor alleged that the transferee refused to perform the agreement and sought possession, or alternatively payment of the balance and interest.
The transferee argued that sections 39 and 55 of the Indian Contract Act prevented the transferor from ending the contract after the transferee’s failure to perform.
issues.conclusion: The suit was competent because the transferor’s case was that the transferee had refused to perform the agreement.
issues.legal_principle: The Court rejected the contention based on sections 39 and 55 of the Indian Contract Act, holding that it did not prevent the transferor from bringing suit where the transferor alleged that the other party had refused to perform the agreement.

predicates.contract_suit_for_possession_or_payment: The proceeding is a suit seeking possession or payment based on a contract.
predicates.plaintiff_alleged_other_party_refused_pe: The plaintiff alleged that the other party refused to perform the contract.
predicates.suit_competent: The suit is competent to be brought.

issues.definition: A suit seeking possession or payment based on a contract is competent when the plaintiff alleges that the other party refused to perform it.
